result.title: How Short Is Too Short? Length-Conditional Calibration and Abstention for Detecting AI-Generated Text
result.summary: Detectors of AI-generated text are usually tuned and tested on passages of several hundred tokens, yet many real cases are short. We study score-based detection as a function of passage length. We give a closed form for how the false-positive rate of a threshold set on long text changes as length falls, and a formula for the number of tokens a detector needs to reach a target true-positive rate. We calibrate thresholds within length bins with conformal p-values, and we add a bin-level rule that abstains when the detector cannot be informative at that length. On synthetic scores the formulas agree with simulation, and binned calibration holds the false-positive rate at its nominal value at every length. On three zero-shot detectors (log-likelihood, log-rank, Binoculars), three corpora and two open-weight generators, binned calibration gives a mean false-positive rate of 5.0% in every detector-length cell from 10 to 200 tokens, averaged over 300 random document-level resplits. A single threshold set at 200 tokens gives 29% for Binoculars at 10 tokens and about 1% for log-likelihood, as the closed form predicts. No detector reaches an 80% true-positive rate, and the best, Binoculars at 200 tokens, reaches 59%, so the rule abstains in every cell at that floor and releases only the 200-token bins at floors of 0.3 and 0.5.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 AI 生成文本检测器在短文本上的可靠性，给出阈值假阳性率随文本长度缩短而变化的闭式公式及达到目标真阳性率所需 token 数，并用长度分箱的 conformal 校准加「该长度下检测器无信息量则弃答」的分箱规则。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按证据量（长度）刻画可靠性与「信息不足即弃答」的决策框架，可能与 LVR 中基于证据充分性的 STOP 决策及推理预算评价相通，可供核查其分箱校准与弃答阈值能否转成停止准则。
